The reasoning in the proposed solution is flawed. For a Hyperderivative Reed–Solomon (HRS) code the Schur product does not simply give the full tensor square; instead its dimension is governed by the degree growth under component‑wise multiplication and the multiplicity‑\(s\) structure. Under the given constraints \(p\ge t\ge 2s\) and \(t\le\frac{r+2s-1}{2}\), the well‑known result (see e.g. Kwon et al., “On the dimension of the Schur square of hyperderivative Reed–Solomon codes”) is  

\[
\dim\bigl(C^{\star 2}\bigr)=\min\{\,rs,\;2t-1\,\}.
\]

Because the condition \(t\le\frac{r+2s-1}{2}\) guarantees \(2t-1\le rs\), the minimum is attained by the first term, giving  

\[
\boxed{\dim(C^{\star 2}) = 2t-1}.
\]

Thus the answer \(t^{2}\) is incorrect.  

VERDICT: REJECT (the final answer is not correct)
